EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz are at a critical level, with Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters declaring no vessel can pass without Iranian authorization, and Emirati oil company ADNOC reporting two of its ships were attacked there. This coincides with the US Defense Secretary asserting indefinite naval blockade capabilities against Iran and the US CENTCOM announcing a new offensive drone unit, raising immediate escalation concerns. Meanwhile, Israel conducted targeted strikes in Gaza, eliminating two Hamas commanders, and faced international condemnation for settler violence in the West Bank.

IRAN
Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters announced that no vessel can safely transit the Strait of Hormuz without Iranian authorization and supervision, dismissing US claims of normal traffic as "fabricated lies." Rear Admiral Ali Azmaei of the IRGC Navy Commander reinforced this, declaring the Strait "closed" and under complete Iranian control. US Defense Secretary Hagseth stated the US can maintain its naval blockade of Iran indefinitely. A Washington Post report indicated the US military has lost at least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones, approximately 25% of its fleet, during the war with Iran, with an estimated total damage exceeding $1.3 billion, noting their vulnerability in the Strait of Hormuz area. US CENTCOM announced the formation of a multinational "Falcon Strike" offensive drone unit, which has already been deployed in military operations against Iran and in July attacks on Iranian port facilities. Mohammad Mokhber, an advisor to Iran's Leader, warned that Iran's shift to an "offensive" war strategy, if its conditions are not met, would "undoubtedly change the equations of power in the world." Ebrahim Azizi, Chairman of the Iranian Parliament's National Security Committee, similarly threatened a "firm, decisive response" to any regional instability resulting from foreign influence. Iran's Intelligence Ministry dismantled two Takfiri terrorist cells in Sistan and Baluchistan province, killing two and arresting four members. Internally, Iranian authorities closed at least 42 businesses in 17 cities for not adhering to hijab laws. Reports from Kerman and Mazandaran indicated severe gas shortages and traffic congestion at gas stations, with some gasoline prices reportedly reaching 87,000 Tomans. Iran's Foreign Ministry accused the US and Israel of war crimes, citing attacks on Minab students, Qeshm residential homes, and the Lamerd stadium with cluster munitions. FM Abbas Araghchi warned the US against "bigger miscalculation" over the Strait of Hormuz. OPEC data showed Iran's oil production increased by only 26,000 barrels last month, significantly less than the combined 1.64 million barrel increase from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Iraq.

ISRAEL
The IDF confirmed killing Jamal Mahmoud Abu Kamil, a Hamas commander involved in the October 7, 2023 attack, in a strike in Gaza City. Another Hamas company commander, planning attacks against IDF forces, was killed in an Israeli strike in Khan Younis. Israeli forces captured three wanted Palestinians in Jenin, suspected of planning an "imminent terror attack." A Palestinian operative who crossed the "Yellow Line" in southern Gaza, posing an "immediate threat," was shot by Paratroopers Brigade soldiers. Thousands of tons of military equipment, including D9 bulldozers, Humvees, JLTV armored vehicles, and Oshkosh trucks, arrived at Haifa Port to bolster IDF ground forces. The IDF conducted strikes in southern Lebanon, with explosions reported in the Upper Galilee Council area. In Marah Aqaba, southern Lebanon, IDF forces found RPGs and other weapons, and destroyed a booby-trapped Hezbollah structure. The Ganim settlement in northern Samaria was re-established 20 years after its evacuation. US Ambassador Mike Huckabee publicly condemned recent settler violence in Qusra, West Bank, referring to the perpetrators as "Israeli terrorists" and calling for their removal, while the UK Embassy also condemned West Bank violence and illegal settlements. Defense Minister Israel Katz stated intentions to "destroy Lebanese homes in the south and build settlements in the West Bank." Israeli politicians, including Avigdor Liberman and Gadi Eisenkot, criticized the government's Gaza policy, alleging Hamas is rebuilding its capabilities and that the IDF is restricted in its response, though the Prime Minister's office denied these claims.

GAZA & WEST BANK
IDF operations in Gaza resulted in the killing of Jamal Mahmoud Abu Kamil, a Hamas commander involved in the October 7, 2023 attack, in Gaza City. Another Hamas company commander was killed in an Israeli strike in Khan Younis, with Palestinian media reporting one fatality from an Israeli strike on a motorcycle in the same area. In the West Bank, three Palestinians suspected of planning an "imminent terror attack" were apprehended by Israeli Yamam forces in Jenin. An operative who crossed the "Yellow Line" in southern Gaza was shot by IDF Paratroopers Brigade soldiers after posing an "immediate threat." Israeli lookout soldiers claimed Hamas is testing Israeli responses by approaching the "Yellow Line," a situation described as reminiscent of pre-October 7. However, the Prime Minister's office denied restricting IDF actions against threats. Settlers returned to Qusra, West Bank, with the IDF deploying to protect residents; US Ambassador Mike Huckabee and the UK Embassy condemned the settler violence and illegal settlements, stating they undermine the two-state solution. Defense Minister Israel Katz explicitly stated intentions to "build settlements in the West Bank." Hamas endorsed Iran's vow to keep the Strait of Hormuz closed until a comprehensive regional ceasefire, including an end to the war in Gaza. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs warned that over half of Gaza's population lacks sufficient access to water, sanitation, and hygiene.

LEBANON
The IDF conducted strikes in Lebanon, with explosions heard in the Upper Galilee Council area. In Marah Aqaba, southern Lebanon, IDF forces located and destroyed a booby-trapped Hezbollah structure and discovered RPG rockets and other weapons. Israel stated it would not allow Hezbollah to harm its citizens and would continue operations in coordination with the ceasefire agreement. Defense Minister Israel Katz declared plans to "destroy Lebanese homes in the south." Lebanon's Foreign Ministry condemned Israel's "systematic destruction" in southern Lebanon as a violation of international law. US-mediated discussions are ongoing regarding Hezbollah's disarmament, with Britain, Italy, Switzerland, and Indonesia proposed as verifying troops. Israel has demanded that inspections include private homes. Hamas praised Iran's stance to keep the Strait of Hormuz closed until a regional ceasefire is achieved, including an end to the war in Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Ismail Qaani, commander of the IRGC Quds Force, visited Baghdad, reportedly urging pro-Iranian militias to retain their weapons, which he referred to as "Iranian weapons," and encouraged Iraqi leadership to leverage these militias for pressure on Washington. Iraq's Investigation Committee summoned military commanders to explain why Hashed al-Shaabi (Popular Mobilization Forces) headquarters were not evacuated prior to attacks. Iraq's Prime Minister ordered the creation of a fund to develop Iraqi air defense capabilities. Iraqi forces thwarted an attempt to smuggle 45,000 drug pills from Syria. Saudi Defense Minister affirmed Iraq as a "dear neighbor." Yemen's Houthis claimed two drone attacks on the Saudi Aramco refinery in Jizan. Saudi Arabia is reportedly considering backing a Yemeni ground offensive to retake the Red Sea coast from Houthi forces, particularly after Houthi missiles reportedly killed crew members on a commercial vessel in Bab-el-Mandeb. Reports of a naval clash between Saudi boats and Houthi (Ansar Allah) forces occurred on Yemen's western coast. US forces remain on track to withdraw from Iraq by September 30. Iran's Foreign Ministry reaffirmed that the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights are an "inseparable part of Syria."

GULF STATES
The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned an unspecified attack. ADNOC, the national oil company of Abu Dhabi, reported two of its vessels were attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, with no casualties. Yemen's Houthis claimed two drone attacks on the Saudi Aramco refinery in Jizan. Following these attacks, Saudi Arabia reportedly closed Abha International Airport, Jizan International Airport, and Najran International Airport. Saudi Arabia is considering supporting a Yemeni ground offensive to recapture the Red Sea coast from Houthi forces. Reports of a naval clash between Saudi boats and Houthi (Ansar Allah) forces occurred on Yemen's western coast. Egypt and UAE Foreign Ministers engaged in a telephone conversation, calling for the US and Iran to return to their June memorandum to de-escalate tensions and prevent the conflict's spread. Oman and Saudi Arabia have reportedly initiated a new project to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. There are unverified claims that the UAE released billions in frozen Iranian assets, possibly in exchange for Iran exempting the UAE from future attacks. An Abu Dhabi energy company is reportedly purchasing Iraqi crude and transporting it through the Strait of Hormuz.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Strait of Hormuz Assertions and Attacks**: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters declared no vessel can safely transit the Strait of Hormuz without Iranian authorization, while ADNOC reported two of its ships were attacked there.
2.  **US Military Posture and Losses**: US Defense Secretary Hagseth affirmed the ability to maintain an indefinite naval blockade of Iran. The US military has lost at least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones (25% of its fleet) in the Iran war, and US CENTCOM announced a new multinational "Falcon Strike" offensive drone unit, already used against Iran.
3.  **Iran's Escalation Warnings**: Mohammad Mokhber, an aide to Iran's Leader, warned of an "offensive" war strategy if Iran's conditions are not met, which he claims would "alter global power equations."
4.  **Hamas Commanders Eliminated**: The IDF killed Hamas commander Jamal Mahmoud Abu Kamil (involved in Oct 7) in Gaza City and another Hamas company commander in Khan Younis.
5.  **Settler Violence Condemned**: US Ambassador Mike Huckabee called for the removal of "Israeli terrorists" (settlers) from Qusra, West Bank, with the UK Embassy also condemning West Bank violence and illegal settlements.
6.  **Ganim Settlement Re-established**: The Ganim settlement was re-established in northern Samaria, 20 years after its evacuation, under the leadership of Yossi Dagan and Minister Smotrich.
7.  **Saudi Airport Closures**: Saudi Arabia reportedly closed Abha, Jizan, and Najran International Airports following Houthi drone attacks on the Jizan Aramco refinery.
8.  **Iran-US Ceasefire Talks Stalled**: Reuters reported no progress in Iran-US talks to extend the June ceasefire, with both sides blaming the other for non-compliance with commitments.
9.  **Oman-Saudi Hormuz Bypass Project**: Oman and Saudi Arabia have initiated a new project aimed at bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks in the Strait of Hormuz are critically high, with Iran's assertive declarations of control and threats of "decisive response" against foreign influence, coupled with reported attacks on Emirati vessels. The US posture of an indefinite naval blockade and deployment of offensive drone units increases the potential for direct military confrontation. The re-establishment of the Ganim settlement and Defense Minister Israel Katz's statements on destroying Lebanese homes and expanding West Bank settlements signal a high likelihood of increased conflict intensity and geographical spread. Reports of Hamas rebuilding power in Gaza and "Yellow Line" incursions suggest a significant risk of renewed or intensified conflict in the Gaza Strip. Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and Saudi consideration of a ground offensive in Yemen point to a high risk of escalation in the Yemen conflict, potentially drawing in more regional actors. The impending US withdrawal from Iraq by September 30 could contribute to regional instability, especially given the IRGC Quds Force's reported encouragement for militias to retain weapons and pressure Washington.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** Defense Secretary Hagseth affirmed indefinite naval blockade capabilities against Iran. Jared Kushner is slated to visit Israel next week for Gaza talks. US CENTCOM announced a new multinational "Falcon Strike" drone unit, already used against Iran. US lawmakers expressed concern over the USS Abraham Lincoln's crew morale. US Ambassador Mike Huckabee condemned "Israeli terrorists" (settlers) in Qusra and called for their removal. Senior US Senate Democrats called for Defense Secretary Hagseth to testify on civilian casualties from US strikes in Iran (Minab school) and Yemen.
**Gulf States**, including the UAE and Egypt, urged the US and Iran to return to their June memorandum for de-escalation. Oman and Saudi Arabia are collaborating on a project to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia closed three international airports (Abha, Jizan, Najran) after Houthi attacks and is considering backing a Yemeni ground offensive.
The **UK Embassy in Israel** condemned West Bank violence and illegal settlements.
**Russia** and Iran are expanding information security cooperation.
**Hamas** praised Iran's vow to keep the Strait of Hormuz closed until a regional ceasefire is achieved in Gaza and Lebanon.
**Lebanon's** Foreign Ministry condemned Israel's "systematic destruction" in the south.
**Colombia** received an Israeli rescue and humanitarian aid delegation.
**Israel** is in talks with Britain, Italy, Switzerland, and Indonesia regarding their potential contribution of troops to verify Hezbollah's disarmament in southern Lebanon.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
**Contradictory Narratives on Gaza Operations**: There is a notable contradiction in reports regarding IDF rules of engagement in Gaza. Israeli lookout soldiers claim they are identifying Hamas activity near the "Yellow Line" but are denied authorization to neutralize threats, leading to a situation described as "like before October 7." The Prime Minister's office and Defense Minister, however, deny any restrictions, asserting that all IDF-submitted targets have been approved.
**Strait of Hormuz Messaging**: Iranian declarations of absolute control over the Strait of Hormuz, labeling US claims of normal maritime traffic as "fabricated lies," present a strong, almost propagandistic, stance aimed at asserting sovereignty and projecting strength. This contrasts sharply with US assurances of freedom of navigation and an indefinite blockade.
**Unverified Claims**: Unconfirmed reports include the alleged release of billions in frozen Iranian assets by the UAE in exchange for exemption from future attacks, and the claimed death of a Basiji named "Saeed Kazemi." Previous reports of Mossad involvement in the search for missing Israelis in Vienna were later denied by other sources. A vague report of an "electricity cut off" in west Tehran following a "very strong sound" lacks sufficient detail for confirmation within the regional conflict context.
**Propaganda Indicators**: Both Iranian and Israeli officials employ highly charged language (e.g., "powerful Armed Forces," "war crimes," "Israeli terrorists," "destroy Lebanese homes") which appears designed to bolster domestic and regional support while demonizing adversaries, rather than conveying objective information. The contrasting accounts concerning the morale and conditions of the USS Abraham Lincoln's crew between US officials and media reports could also indicate efforts at information management.
**Reporting Gaps**: Specific details regarding the perpetrators and exact nature of the ADNOC ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz are not provided. The precise scope and potential targets of Iran's threatened "offensive" strategy remain unspecified. Details regarding the new Oman-Saudi project to bypass the Strait of Hormuz are sparse. The exact demands and parameters for Israel's proposed inspections of private homes in Lebanon for Hezbollah disarmament are also not fully elaborated.
